business_problem: The Paris 2024 organizing committee needed to personalize fan communications for millions of contacts while also integrating athlete accreditation, medical, logistics, and performance data across many event systems.
solution_summary: Paris 2024 used the Salesforce Platform to unify fan, athlete, and operations data for one of the largest live events in the world, combining Marketing Cloud, Journey Builder, MuleSoft, and Tableau in a shared event architecture. A fan database built from social engagement, website subscriptions, and ticket purchases fed Journey Builder workflows that collected preferences, segmented audiences, and delivered tailored greetings and updates across 70 journeys in five languages. Marketing Cloud handled the high-volume email and SMS outreach, while MuleSoft connected accreditation data, electronic medical records, customs verification, laundry systems, and weather feeds so athletes and organizers could access the right services during the Games. Tableau added a performance analytics layer for athletes by turning sensor data into training insights, giving the committee a single platform for both fan engagement and event-time operational decision-making.
data_flow: Fan data from social channels, website subscriptions, and ticketing feeds into Salesforce and Journey Builder for segmentation and outreach, while MuleSoft connects accreditation, EMR, customs, laundry, and weather systems into event workflows and Tableau turns operational or athlete sensor data into dashboards.
business_outcome: Paris 2024 personalized outreach for millions of fans, delivered athlete-service integrations during the Games, and gave organizers and athletes a stronger analytics layer for both logistics and performance tuning.
metrics: 25.2 million emails sent during the Olympics
8.9 million SMS messages sent during the Olympics (96.4% delivery rate)
48 cases (including eight critical cases) to resolution
architecture_clues: Journey Builder starts with a welcome email and preference survey before routing fans into sport-specific journeys.
MuleSoft validates athlete access to venues, services, customs workflows, and weather feeds during the Games.
Tableau used body and equipment sensors to analyze wheelchair tennis serve mechanics.
evidence_quotes: The Salesforce Platform allowed the Paris 2024 committee to create a single view of each of its 8 million fans.
Based on their answers, fans received tailored greetings, questionnaires, and updates about their favorite sports through 70 different journeys in five languages.
Throughout the 16 days of the Olympic Games, the organization sent 25.2 million emails and 8.9 million SMS messages.
MuleSoft also integrated with external systems like Paris 2024's electronic medical records system (EMR).
